record.paper_title: Gradings, Braidings, Representations, Paraparticles: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF and PFB, which gradings by small finite abelian groups preserve the algebraic or coalgebraic structure? More concretely, for groups such as Z2, Z3, Z4, and Z2 × Z2, classify the group actions or coactions that turn these paraparticle algebras into graded module algebras or graded module coalgebras.

evidence.quote: 1st Research Objective: The first problem we intend to investigate is the classification of the gradings induced on the paraparticle (co)algebras (especially on PBF and PFB algebras) by small order finite Abelian Groups such as Z2, Z3, Z4, Z2 × Z2 etc. In other words, we intend to classify those group (co)actions which preserve the corresponding (co)algebra structures, turning thus the (co)algebras in CG-(co)module (co)algebras.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let $\mathbb{C}$ be the ground field. The relative parabose-fermi algebra $P_{BF}$ and the relative parafermi-bose algebra $P_{FB}$ are the unital associative $\mathbb{C}$-algebras defined as follows.

Fix positive integers $m,n$ and generators $\{b_i^+, b_i^- : i=1,\dots,m\}$ ("para-bose") and $\{f_j^+, f_j^- : j=1,\dots,n\}$ ("para-fermi"). For $\xi,\eta,\varepsilon\in\{+,-\}$ write $[x,y]=xy-yx$ and $\{x,y\}=xy+yx$.

The algebra $P_{BF}$ is generated by these symbols subject to the (Greenberg–Messiah) trilinear relations
\[
[\{b_i^\xi,b_j^\eta\},b_k^\varepsilon]=2\delta_{jk}(\varepsilon-\eta)\,b_i^\xi\delta_{\xi\varepsilon}\cdots
\]
(the standard parabose triple relations among the $b$'s), the standard parafermi triple relations
\[
[[f_i^\xi,f_j^\eta],f_k^\varepsilon]=2\delta_{jk}\delta_{\eta,-\varepsilon}\eta\,f_i^\xi-2\delta_{ik}\delta_{\xi,-\varepsilon}\xi\,f_j^\eta
\]
among the $f$'s, together with the mixed "relative" commutation relations
\[
[b_i^\xi,f_j^\eta]=0\qquad\text{for all }i,j,\xi,\eta,
\]
i.e. paraboson and parafermion sectors mutually commute. The algebra $P_{FB}$ is defined identically except that the mixed sector relations are replaced by the anticommuting relations
\[
\{b_i^\xi,f_j^\eta\}-\text{appropriate trilinear corrections}=0,
\]
so that the two sectors anticommute (the "relative" parafermi-bose case). Both algebras carry natural Hopf-algebra-like (super)bialgebra structures: a coproduct, counit and antipode making them braided graded module bialgebras in suitable braided categories.

Problem.

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and write $\mathbb{C}G$ for its group algebra and $(\mathbb{C}G)^*$ for its dual Hopf algebra. A $G$-grading of an associative algebra $A$ that respects its (co)algebra structure means a $\mathbb{C}G$-module algebra structure (equivalently a $G$-action by algebra automorphisms) on $A$, or dually a $\mathbb{C}G$-comodule coalgebra structure (a $G$-grading of the underlying coalgebra) such that the coproduct, counit and antipode become $G$-graded maps.

Classify, up to equivalence, all $G$-actions and all $G$-coactions on $P_{BF}$ and on $P_{FB}$ that turn these algebras into $\mathbb{C}G$-module algebras and $\mathbb{C}G$-comodule coalgebras, respectively, for each of the small finite abelian groups
\[
G\in\{\mathbb{Z}_2,\;\mathbb{Z}_3,\;\mathbb{Z}_4,\;\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2\}.
\]
Equivalently, classify all gradings $P_{BF}=\bigoplus_{g\in G}(P_{BF})_g$ and $P_{FB}=\bigoplus_{g\in G}(P_{FB})_g$ that are compatible simultaneously with the algebra and coalgebra structures of these paraparticle (co)algebras.
artifact.status_search_result: No published classification of finite abelian group gradings on the relative paraparticle algebras P_BF and P_FB was located. The problem is stated as a research objective and subsequent literature on these specific algebras does not appear to provide a full classification, so the problem appears to remain open.
